rawFindings.title: do_auth command error now emits 'error' event instead of callback invocation
rawFindings.explanation: Previously, if authentication failed due to an error other than 'LOADING' or 'no password is set', the authentication callback (if any) was called with the error. After the change, the error is emitted on the client instance and the callback (auth_callback) is not called. This breaks the contract that an auth callback provided to do_auth will be called on error, causing potential confusion or missed error handling in user code that relies on the callback.
rawFindings.suggestion: Invoke the auth_callback with the error if it is defined, before emitting the error event. This preserves backward compatibility and ensures errors are reported via callback as expected.
rawFindings.failureAfterChange: Calling client.auth with a bad password and a callback causes the callback not to be invoked on error, but an 'error' event is emitted instead, which may cause unhandled errors or test failures expecting the callback.

rawFindings.title: do_auth error callback calls auth_callback with error but successful callback with null error
rawFindings.explanation: Changed 'self.auth_callback(err, res);' to 'self.auth_callback(null, res);' which is correct and fixes the previous bug where the callback incorrectly received an error even on success.
rawFindings.suggestion: No fix needed; this is an improvement.

rawFindings.title: return_error method sets err.command_used to upper case of command
rawFindings.explanation: The error passed to return_error now gets a 'command_used' property set to the uppercased command that caused the error. This can help error handlers detect which command failed. No negative impact expected.
rawFindings.suggestion: No fix needed; this is an enhancement.
